scenes.tts: How can one fatty acid become roughly one hundred six A T P? Watch a sixteen-carbon chain enter this mitochondrial workshop, then count what leaves.
scenes.caption: How can one fatty acid become roughly 106 ATP? Watch a 16-carbon chain enter this mitochondrial workshop, then count what leaves.
scenes.visual: Hook inside one persistent, full-frame schematic mitochondrial workshop. A thick chain of 16 numbered blocks snakes in from a large fat droplet at left toward a central circular processing wheel; an empty ATP gauge and three empty product counters sit at right. During the first question, the chain stretches to fill 60% of the frame height and the gauge flickers between question marks. During 'Watch,' the chain begins moving toward the wheel, the title 'The Two-Carbon Ledger' writes above it, and the three counters pulse without revealing answers. Keep matrix particles drifting and the wheel turning slowly throughout. Labels are at least 28 px; no molecular structures.
scenes.narration: How can one fatty acid become roughly 106 ATP? Watch a 16-carbon chain enter this mitochondrial workshop, then count what leaves.

scenes.tts: In its simplest form, beta oxidation handles a saturated, even-numbered chain. Fat stores many electrons on carbon-hydrogen bonds. The workshop harvests them while removing two carbons per turn. First, however, the chain must reach the machinery.
scenes.caption: In its simplest form, β-oxidation handles a saturated, even-numbered chain. Fat stores many electrons on carbon–hydrogen bonds. The workshop harvests them while removing two carbons per turn. First, however, the chain must reach the machinery.
scenes.visual: Carry forward the same workshop and 16-block chain. On 'simplest form,' a brace marked 'saturated · even chain' settles over the chain while a small corner label reads 'schematic.' On 'electrons,' bright dots travel along the chain blocks toward the central wheel and make the empty ATP gauge glow, without adding a number. On 'two carbons,' the wheel briefly groups the first two blocks with a moving bracket, then releases them back so no product is claimed yet. On the final sentence, pan left with the still-moving chain toward the droplet and blood corridor; keep the wheel rotating in the background.
scenes.narration: In its simplest form, β-oxidation handles a saturated, even-numbered chain. Fat stores many electrons on carbon–hydrogen bonds. The workshop harvests them while removing two carbons per turn. First, however, the chain must reach the machinery.

scenes.tts: During fasting or exercise, fat droplets release fatty acids into blood. Albumin carries them to energy-using tissues. Activation attaches coenzyme A and spends two A T P equivalents. Long-chain cargo then crosses the inner membrane through the carnitine shuttle.
scenes.caption: During fasting or exercise, fat droplets release fatty acids into blood. Albumin carries them to energy-using tissues. Activation attaches coenzyme A and spends two ATP equivalents. Long-chain cargo then crosses the inner membrane through the carnitine shuttle.
scenes.visual: Continue in the left side of the same world. On 'release,' one labelled chain slides out of the large droplet into a wide blood lane while the droplet gently ripples. On 'Albumin,' a large carrier cart labelled 'albumin' catches the chain and rolls toward the mitochondrial wall. At 'Activation,' the chain clips onto a CoA-labelled handle while ONE gold ATP token drops into a toll slot and breaks into AMP plus two phosphate chips, so the ledger reads 'minus 2 ATP equivalents' (one ATP, two bonds; never draw two ATP). On 'Long-chain cargo,' at the outer membrane bar the CoA handle is swapped for a 'carnitine' handle; the carnitine-carried chain crosses the inner membrane bar, where a matrix CoA handle replaces carnitine, and carnitine returns empty. The CoA handle never crosses. The camera follows every transfer; label the whole sequence 'schematic.'
scenes.narration: During fasting or exercise, fat droplets release fatty acids into blood. Albumin carries them to energy-using tissues. Activation attaches coenzyme A and spends two ATP equivalents. Long-chain cargo then crosses the inner membrane through the carnitine shuttle.

scenes.tts: Inside the matrix, count from the coenzyme A end. Carbon two is alpha, and carbon three is beta. A plain chain offers no cutting handle. Three moves rebuild the beta carbon, preparing the bond beside it.
scenes.caption: Inside the matrix, count from the coenzyme A end. Carbon 2 is α, and carbon 3 is β. A plain chain offers no cutting handle. Three moves rebuild the β-carbon, preparing the bond beside it.
scenes.visual: Rebuild the same chain large across the matrix floor with the CoA handle fixed at left. A moving counting cursor lands on blocks 1, 2 and 3 in order; blocks 2 and 3 gain large alpha and beta badges as named. A pair of blunt scissor jaws approaches the bond beside block 3, slips off, and opens again to show the cutting problem. During 'Three moves,' three empty stations rotate into the central wheel around block 3; the beta badge rides with that block. Matrix particles and a slow conveyor keep moving. This is a labelled-block cartoon, not a molecular structure.
scenes.narration: Inside the matrix, count from the coenzyme A end. Carbon 2 is α, and carbon 3 is β. A plain chain offers no cutting handle. Three moves rebuild the β-carbon, preparing the bond beside it.

scenes.tts: First oxidation makes a double bond and reduces F A D to F A D H two. Hydration adds water, placing an O H on the beta carbon. Second oxidation makes a ketone and reduces N A D plus to N A D H. Now thiolase can cut.
scenes.caption: First oxidation makes a double bond and reduces FAD to FADH₂. Hydration adds water, placing an OH on the β-carbon. Second oxidation makes a ketone and reduces NAD⁺ to NADH. Now thiolase can cut.
scenes.visual: The central wheel now performs three continuous transformations on the carried block chain. At 'First oxidation,' station one places a badge labelled 'double bond' over blocks 2 and 3 while an FAD counter flips to FADH₂ and rolls right. At 'Hydration,' a blue water drop enters station two and block 3 receives a large OH badge. At 'Second oxidation,' station three transforms that badge into a cutting handle labelled 'ketone' while an NAD⁺ counter flips to NADH and rolls right. On 'thiolase,' the formerly slipping jaws grip the new handle and begin closing. Keep the conveyor, counters and wheel moving; mark all chemistry 'schematic.' Use labelled blocks only, never molecular bonds or structures.
scenes.narration: First oxidation makes a double bond and reduces FAD to FADH₂. Hydration adds water, placing an OH on the β-carbon. Second oxidation makes a ketone and reduces NAD⁺ to NADH. Now thiolase can cut.

scenes.tts: Thiolase adds fresh coenzyme A and releases one two-carbon acetyl coenzyme A. The remaining chain is two carbons shorter, so it returns to the first step. Beta oxidation converts chain length into a ledger of turns, carrier pairs, and acetyl coenzyme A.
scenes.caption: Thiolase adds fresh coenzyme A and releases one two-carbon acetyl-CoA. The remaining chain is two carbons shorter, so it returns to the first step. β-oxidation converts chain length into a ledger of turns, carrier pairs, and acetyl-CoA.
scenes.visual: Complete the cut in the same workshop. On 'fresh coenzyme A,' a second CoA handle arrives on a moving arm. The jaws close; the two front blocks leave with the ORIGINAL CoA handle as an acetyl-CoA cart rolling to the right counter, and the fresh handle clips onto the shortened chain's new front end. The shortened chain visibly has 14 blocks and loops back around the wheel as the turn counter advances to 1. While the guiding idea is spoken, the chain continues circling slowly and three synchronized ledger columns rise: 'turns,' 'carrier pairs,' and 'acetyl-CoA.' Transform the three wheel stations into those columns rather than cutting to a new layout.
scenes.narration: Thiolase adds fresh coenzyme A and releases one two-carbon acetyl-CoA. The remaining chain is two carbons shorter, so it returns to the first step. β-oxidation converts chain length into a ledger of turns, carrier pairs, and acetyl-CoA.

scenes.tts: Predict the palmitate ledger. A sixteen-carbon chain becomes how many two-carbon acetyl coenzyme A units, after how many turns? Place your answer beside the empty counters.
scenes.caption: Predict the palmitate ledger. A 16-carbon chain becomes how many 2-carbon acetyl-CoA units, after how many turns? Place your answer beside the empty counters.
scenes.visual: The carried 16-block chain straightens across the upper half of the workshop. Below it, two large counters labelled 'turns = ?' and 'acetyl-CoA = ?' grow to fill the lower half. As the question is asked, a glowing two-block bracket travels from left to right along the chain, then resets and travels again. The wheel turns faintly behind the counters, and the ATP gauge remains at 'minus 2' without revealing the answer.
scenes.narration: Predict the palmitate ledger. A 16-carbon chain becomes how many 2-carbon acetyl-CoA units, after how many turns? Place your answer beside the empty counters.

scenes.visual: Hold the exact prediction layout for 4.5 seconds. The question and both empty counters remain unchanged. The two-block bracket continues sweeping along the 16-block chain, a small thinking timer traces one circle, and matrix particles drift; reveal no numbers.

scenes.tts: Eight acetyl coenzyme A units leave, but only seven turns run. Seven cuts make eight pieces, and the last turn releases two acetyl coenzyme A. Therefore, seven F A D H two and seven N A D H also enter the ledger.
scenes.caption: Eight acetyl-CoA units leave, but only seven turns run. Seven cuts make eight pieces, and the last turn releases two acetyl-CoA. Therefore, 7 FADH₂ and 7 NADH also enter the ledger.
scenes.visual: Resolve the prediction without changing worlds. The moving bracket snaps the chain into eight two-block groups while seven thin cut marks appear sequentially. The counters roll to '7 turns' and '8 acetyl-CoA.' On 'last turn,' enlarge the final four-block segment; the wheel splits it once and two acetyl-CoA carts leave together. Then seven FADH₂ tokens and seven NADH tokens stream from the turning wheel into their ledger columns, one matched pair per turn.
scenes.narration: Eight acetyl-CoA units leave, but only seven turns run. Seven cuts make eight pieces, and the last turn releases two acetyl-CoA. Therefore, 7 FADH₂ and 7 NADH also enter the ledger.

scenes.tts: Each carrier pair yields about four A T P through oxidative phosphorylation. Each acetyl coenzyme A yields about ten through the citric acid cycle and oxidative phosphorylation. Seven pairs give twenty-eight; eight acetyl coenzyme A give eighty. Subtract the two-A T P activation toll. The result is roughly one hundred six A T P.
scenes.caption: Each carrier pair yields about 4 ATP through oxidative phosphorylation. Each acetyl-CoA yields about 10 through the citric acid cycle and oxidative phosphorylation. Seven pairs give 28; eight acetyl-CoA give 80. Subtract the 2-ATP activation toll. The result is roughly 106 ATP.
scenes.visual: Carry the three ledger columns to the right side of the workshop and transform the ATP gauge into a large running total, parking the 'minus 2' toll in its slot so the running total starts at 0. Seven carrier-pair tokens roll through a small turbine labelled 'oxidative phosphorylation'; the gauge climbs to 28. Eight acetyl-CoA carts roll through a larger loop labelled 'citric acid cycle + oxidative phosphorylation'; the total climbs to 108. On 'Subtract,' the parked 'minus 2' toll returns from the toll slot and pulls the gauge down to 'roughly 106 ATP.' Keep both machines spinning and token trails moving while each total settles.
scenes.narration: Each carrier pair yields about 4 ATP through oxidative phosphorylation. Each acetyl-CoA yields about 10 through the citric acid cycle and oxidative phosphorylation. Seven pairs give 28; eight acetyl-CoA give 80. Subtract the 2-ATP activation toll. The result is roughly 106 ATP.

scenes.tts: That count applies to a saturated, even chain burned completely to carbon dioxide. Double bonds and odd chains change the accounting. The reusable rule remains. Count the turns, the acetyl coenzyme A, and the activation toll.
scenes.caption: That count applies to a saturated, even chain burned completely to carbon dioxide. Double bonds and odd chains change the accounting. The reusable rule remains. Count the turns, the acetyl-CoA, and the activation toll.
scenes.visual: Zoom back to the full persistent workshop. The completed 16-block chain ledger remains bright at center with a scope ribbon reading 'saturated · even · complete oxidation.' Two dim side chains labelled 'double bonds' and 'odd chains' bend toward open question marks, clearly outside today's computed total. During the final rule, the central wheel, product counters and minus-two toll transform into three large moving icons: a turning wheel, stacked acetyl-CoA carts, and one ATP token cracking to AMP, tagged 'minus 2.' The 106 gauge glows behind them.
scenes.narration: That count applies to a saturated, even chain burned completely to carbon dioxide. Double bonds and odd chains change the accounting. The reusable rule remains. Count the turns, the acetyl-CoA, and the activation toll.

scenes.visual: End card on the same dark ground. Hex waves above the line 'Count the turns, the acetyl-CoA, and the activation toll.' The three matching icons from the workshop drift gently beneath the line; no title is repeated.
